title: {Syn} FFT Turns Convolution Into Pointwise Multiplication
content:
The fast Fourier transform computes a discrete Fourier transform in O(n log n) time instead of O(n^2). It is one of the great algorithmic speedups of the twentieth century.

FFT powers signal processing, image analysis, polynomial multiplication, audio tools, and many scientific simulations.

Why it matters: algorithms keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
